correctness.rationale: The field F4, 20 lines and 80 forbidden triples are exactly specified; line-derived and determinant-derived forbidden triples agree. Enumeration gives 1792 nonempty faces, f=(16,120,480,840,288,48), and 120 four-point and 48 six-point maximal faces. The embedded certificate contains 783 disjoint face-cover pairs, whose induced orientation of all 6768 Hasse incidences is acyclic by exhaustive 1792-node topological sort. Unmatched faces are exactly one vertex and 225 three-simplices; the discrete-Morse CW theorem therefore gives a wedge of 225 three-spheres. Actual packaged files are rechecked and executable verifier run before delivery; no homology-only shortcut.

originality.rationale: The exact-object 2018 thesis gives precisely the known face vector (16,120,480,840,288,48) and reduced integral H_3=Z^225, but neither a homotopy equivalence nor an acyclic matching. Full available text of the older 2013 incidence-geometric paper and accessible full HTML text of the 2016 maximal-arc paper study different invariants. Indexed searches under cap, arc, no-three-collinear, and hypergraph general-position aliases did not find an explicit or stronger theorem implying the new sphere-wedge homotopy classification. The novelty is exclusively this homotopy refinement, not the table. Residual risk of an unindexed equivalent remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently titled source could independently contain this homotopy equivalence; indexed searches do not establish absolute novelty.

The existing exact same-object integral homology and face-vector table substantially reduces the incremental contribution; the only original claim here is the stronger homotopy type and explicit matching.

The available indexed descriptions of affine-plane incidence Vietoris–Rips complexes were not full-text verified because they refer to a different simplicial face construction; no claim of exhaustive literature coverage is made.

value.rationale: The object is the complete no-three-collinear simplicial complex of the smallest nonprime affine plane, a natural nonpure finite-geometric object with maximal caps of four and six points. Published integral Betti numbers and face counts do not determine a 5-dimensional complex up to homotopy. A complete explicit acyclic matching resolves that gap, showing it is a 3-sphere wedge without hidden higher attaching maps; the precise homotopy type is useful for topological comparison of affine/projective cap complexes and future equivariant study. No general larger-order theorem is claimed.
